title: Operating courtesy, band plans and RACES
blurb: Share frequencies politely, space signals correctly, follow band plans, respond to distress, and know the RACES rules.

G2B01.why: Outside emergencies, **no station has priority** on any frequency. Nets, QSOs and contests all share.
G2B01.trap: Being first, or running a net, gives no right to the frequency.

G2B02.why: A distress call outranks your contact. **Acknowledge** that station and **find out what help is needed**.
G2B02.trap: Going silent or cutting power doesn't help anyone in distress.

G2B03.why: Nobody has priority, so **work it out** with the other stations in a **mutually acceptable** way.
G2B03.trap: Claiming priority or flipping sideband just creates more interference.

G2B04.why: CW is narrow, so **150 to 500 Hz** between stations avoids interference.
G2B04.trap: 2 to 3 kHz is the SSB spacing.

G2B05.why: SSB is about 3 kHz wide, so leave **2 to 3 kHz** between stations.
G2B05.trap: 150 to 500 Hz is only enough for narrow CW signals.

G2B06.why: Ask first: **"QRL?" plus your call** on CW, or ask if the frequency is in use plus your call on phone.
G2B06.trap: QSY means changing frequency, so it doesn't ask if the frequency is busy.

G2B07.why: The **voluntary band plan** is how amateurs agree where to operate. Following it is accepted practice.

G2B08.why: **50.100 to 50.125 MHz** is the DX window: only contacts with stations **outside the 48 contiguous states**.

G2B09.why: A RACES control operator must **hold an FCC-issued amateur operator license**. A non-licensed official doesn't qualify.

G2B10.why: Interference and conditions change, so a net should have a **backup frequency**.
G2B10.trap: Reading the whole roster or repeating phonetics wastes air time.

G2B11.why: Routine RACES drills and tests are limited to **1 hour per week** without special authorization.
